story.A: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books a first express facial with Jess at Lee Skin Studio, for Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am, and fills in the skin form on the secure page. A first peel needs a patch test 48 hours before and Jess's OK on the form, and takes a $40 deposit. Pick a money choice at the top to follow its path.
story.B: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books Lee Mobile Skin for a home facial at 26 Aspen Ct, and Mateo comes Thu Oct 22 between 8 and 10am. The service depends on the money choice you pick: a home facial, or a bridal spa morning for 5, two days before a Saturday wedding, priced from the host's answers.

pf.license.need: always: esthetics (facials, waxing, light peels) is licensed where the state's rules require it
pf.license.who: both: the studio holds an establishment license where the state issues one, and each esthetician holds their own
pf.license.ask: the studio's license number; each esthetician's number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it)
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.scope: the services each license covers, from the state's form: lasers, injections, microneedling and deep peels are medical treatments in many states, so they're never listed for an esthetics business; a service no license on file covers can't be listed
pf.license.away: facials and waxing at a home or a venue only where the state's rules allow esthetics away from a licensed establishment; some states ask for an extra permit (a switch from the state form)
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: liability insurance where the state's form asks for it
pf.license.roomRenter: an esthetician who rents a room is their own business: their own license, prices and Stripe
pf.license.lashBrow: lash and brow work is its own kind of work, with its own license where the state asks

pf.services.notOffered: lasers, injections, microneedling and deep peels: medical treatments, done at a med spa; Rosie points the customer there
pf.services.capacity: one esthetician and one treatment room per booking; a spa party is one booking with several guests and one code
pf.services.buffer: 15 minutes after each visit to clean and reset the room
pf.services.gaps: no waxing within 7 days of a peel (the example studio's rule): times too close to the customer's other bookings aren't offered
pf.services.skills: facials, waxing, peels, corrective facials; only estheticians trained in peels are offered for peels
pf.services.online: no: treatments are done in person
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the customer is the one treated

beforeTimes: the service, and what it should help with: dullness, breakouts, dark spots, texture, or hair removal
skin type: dry, oily, combination or sensitive
a first peel here, or not
who it's for: me, or my child under 18
afterTime: anything the esthetician should know that isn't private, like a scent you don't like
for a home visit: the address, parking, and a quiet room with space for a treatment bed and a plug
securePage: only what the chosen service needs, never through the AI
isotretinoin (an acne medicine) in the last 6 months
retinoids, and the last time used
pregnant or breastfeeding (asked for peels only)
laser, peel, waxing or injections in the last 2 weeks
a cold sore, rash, sunburn or broken skin now
pf.questions.rulesOut: isotretinoin in the last 6 months rules out waxing and peels (the medicine's label warns against both), so the page offers a gentle facial at the same time instead; pregnancy, an allergy or a flare-up waits for the esthetician to decide
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18, who books, fills in the form, signs the consent, comes to every visit and stays in the room for any waxing (and any older age or written OK where the state's rules require it)

stop.words: a reaction happening now: face, lips or throat swelling, or trouble breathing
a burn or blistering from a product
stop.say: Rinse with cool water, and see a doctor or urgent care today.
stop.booking: no booking until the skin has healed

goOn.words: a cold sore, a rash, broken skin or a sunburn on the area
goOn.what: no peel or wax on that skin; the esthetician re-checks the skin, the form and any patch-test spot before treating; if it isn't ready: a gentle facial or a new date, with no fee

pf.safety.after: a reaction after a treatment (redness, burning): the safety text first; then the esthetician is asked to call within the hour, and the owner gets the same text after 15 minutes with no answer; Rosie never says whether a reaction is normal
pf.safety.always: the generic screen: danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency → call 911, and no booking

steps.name: Patch test (a small dab of the peel on the skin, to check for a reaction)
steps.when: at least 48 hours before a first peel; free, 15 minutes, booked as a linked visit
steps.who: a first peel, and anyone whose last test has run out
steps.goodFor: 3 months (the example studio's rule), with any esthetician on the team
steps.result: the customer watches the spot; any change: reply to the reminder, and the esthetician calls; she decides: the peel goes ahead, a gentle facial instead (deposit counted, no fee), or no treatment (full refund)

steps.name: Skin form and treatment consent
steps.when: on the secure page before the first visit, and again before every peel; due now, inside the saved time
steps.who: every new client; a parent signs for a minor
steps.goodFor: on file for later facials and waxing, with a short 'anything changed?' check on the page
steps.result: answers that rule a service out offer a gentle facial; a first peel's form is read by the esthetician before it's booked

pf.first_steps.reaction: a past reaction to a peel or wax: the booking waits for the esthetician's OK; the reason stays in the record, never in a text
pf.first_steps.prep: peel prep: no retinol, other retinoids or exfoliating acids on the face for 5 days before, no facial waxing for 7 days before, and no sunburn; a prescribed retinoid: ask the prescriber before pausing it; sent at booking when the peel is 7 days away or less, and again with the reminder. Waxing: let the hair grow about a quarter inch. A facial needs no prep.

pf.visit.checkIn: at the studio: the check-in code at the front desk or in the treatment room; at a home or venue: the code at the door, from the customer or the host
pf.visit.beforeWork: the esthetician goes over the skin form with the customer, looks at the skin and any patch-test spot, and asks what's changed; skin that isn't ready gets a gentle facial or a new date, with no fee
pf.visit.changes: extra work (an add-on mask, extractions, a lip wax) is priced and OK'd before it's done; a corrective facial is priced after the skin check, with the customer's yes first
pf.visit.done: the check-in code, or DONE from the esthetician; the treatment, products and minutes go in the customer's private record; the aftercare note follows
pf.visit.away: at a home or venue, the esthetician brings the treatment bed, towels and products; the customer gives a quiet room with a plug

pf.money.before: facials and waxing: a card saved for the $20 fee (nothing taken for a returning client's quick wax, as the owner sets); the Intro facial for new clients: paid in full when booking; a peel: a $40 deposit, counted toward the bill; a corrective facial: the $25 consult as a deposit toward the price, never more than its starting price; home visits: a card saved for the $89 trip fee, charged only for a late cancel or a missed visit; spa parties: a 25% deposit
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form
pf.money.cancel: free to cancel until 24 hours before a studio visit, and until 7am on the day of a home visit (the owner's settings)
pf.money.fees: late cancel or no-show: $20 ($40 for a peel, $89 for a home visit); the owner confirms each fee, never more than what was agreed
pf.money.refunds: a full refund, with no fee, when the studio changes the plan, a patch test or a skin reason changes it, or a free patch test is missed
pf.money.tips: on: at the desk, or a tip line on the bill Rosie texts; tips go to the esthetician
pf.money.tax: a tax line for skin care products sold, where the state's rules require it

pf.messages.never: nothing from a skin form (medicines, pregnancy, allergies, skin conditions, patch-test results) goes in a text or through the AI: only the secure page and the customer's record; staff open forms only by a secure link after signing in
pf.messages.notes: prep and aftercare notes are the same for every client of a service; a skin question by text gets a call from the esthetician, never a texted answer
pf.messages.private: an intimate wax shows only as a wax in texts, and a customer can ask for texts with only the business, date, time and place
pf.messages.minors: a minor's booking texts go to the parent or guardian, never to the teen; data about a minor is never used for marketing

pf.staff.licenses: each esthetician's own license per state; lash and brow work where the state licenses it apart
pf.staff.skills: facials, waxing, peels, corrective facials; only estheticians trained in peels are offered for peels
pf.staff.supervision: apprentices and students work only under a licensed esthetician, where the state's rules allow
pf.staff.oks: the esthetician reads every first-peel skin form before it's booked (only a first peel waits; facials and waxing book at once); no reply in 2 hours: the owner is asked, and whoever answers first decides; a skin change or a reaction: the esthetician calls and decides, never the AI
pf.staff.standIn: a stand-in gets the skin form, the patch-test date and the last treatment notes; a patch test counts with any esthetician on the team
pf.staff.away: only estheticians cleared for home visits are offered away from the studio

pf.rules.showLicense: the license is shown where the state asks: posted at the studio, on the listing, in confirmations, or in the text that moves a booking to another esthetician (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.scope: the services each esthetics license covers, from the state form
pf.rules.away: work away from the studio only where the state allows it, and only for the services it allows (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.minors: a parent's written OK for waxing a minor, and any older age for minors, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.healthData: Rosie's rule: ask only what the chosen service needs, and keep health answers on the secure page
pf.rules.tips: tips to staff follow the state's tip rules (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.records: skin forms, consents, patch tests and treatment notes kept with the customer's record: 7 years, or longer where the state asks
pf.rules.contracts: a signed agreement for spa parties (the owner's setting), and where the state's rules require one above an amount

pf.edges.lateArrival: 15 minutes' grace; later, the esthetician decides if the full treatment still fits before the next booking; if not, a shorter treatment or a new time; any fee only as the booking terms say, and the owner confirms it
pf.edges.patchTest: a missed patch test: no fee; a new test that still fits 48 hours before the peel, a switch to a gentle facial, or a free cancel; no reply by the evening: the owner calls; no peel without a test
pf.edges.linked: a patch test and its peel are linked: a move keeps the 48 hours, and a cancel takes both
pf.edges.gap: no waxing within 7 days of a peel: those times aren't offered, and one line says why
pf.edges.skinNotReady: skin not ready on the day: a gentle facial or a new date, with no fee
pf.edges.reaction: a reaction after the visit: the safety steps first, then the esthetician's call
pf.edges.standIn: an esthetician out sick: a stand-in with the skill and the notes, or new times with no fee
pf.edges.party: a spa party: one booking, several guests, one check-in code
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way
pf.edges.care: a free follow-up visit within 7 days when the skin feels wrong after a treatment (the example studio's promise)

notes:
Pilot: started from hair (the chair pilot), not dentist. Why: an esthetics studio runs like a salon (a chosen person in a treatment room, a patch test before a first peel, a deposit on the longer treatment, paid at the desk), and it bills no plan or insurance. From dentist it takes only the idea of a form on the secure page: the skin form and consent (A4-72, B4-86), which hair had turned off.
Names: Lee Skin Studio (flow A, 75 Linden St) and Lee Mobile Skin (flow B); estheticians Jess and Nadia at the studio, Mateo and Gwen on the road. Sam's three kinds of work are skin care, lash work and the studio.
Services and prices are the studio's example settings, kept close to the master's numbers so the money lines still add up: Express facial $35, Intro facial $55 (new clients, paid in full), Glow peel $140 with a $40 deposit, Corrective facial from $110 with a $25 consult, Home facial $179 with the $89 trip fee held, Spa party priced from the host's answers ($640 for 5 guests, 25% deposit, Sam OKs over $500).
